title: File is 1678 lines (exceeds 1000-line maintainability guideline)
detail: At 1678 lines this file exceeds the maintainability threshold. Large files blur module responsibilities and slow code review. Fix: split into focused sub-modules.

title: Line 108: broad `except Exception` (BLE001)
detail: Catching `Exception` at line 108 prevents distinguishing expected errors from unexpected failures. Fix: catch specific exception types, or re-raise after logging if a broad catch is intentional.

title: verbose exception re-raise at line 1631
detail: `raise exc` replaces the original exception losing the traceback. Use bare `raise` inside `except` to re-raise with the full chain preserved.

title: 3× broad `except Exception` (W0703) — lines 441, 494, 1360
detail: 3 broad `except Exception` clauses (first at line 441). Each swallows unexpected error types. Fix: catch specific exceptions at each site.

title: 2× exception raised without `from` in except block (W0707, first at line 227)
detail: At 2 location(s) (first at line 227), a new exception is raised inside an `except` block without `raise ... from original_exc`. This discards the original traceback and makes debugging harder. Fix: `raise NewExc(...) from exc` to preserve the chain.

title: Line 1383: inconsistent return statements — some paths return a value, some don't
detail: The function at/near line 1383 has paths that return a value and paths that fall off the end (implicit `return None`). Callers expecting a return value silently receive `None` on the implicit path. Fix: add explicit `return None` or ensure all paths return a consistent type.

title: Builtin `type` shadowed by local variable (W0622)
detail: Local variable(s) at line 323 shadow the builtin(s) type. If the builtin is needed elsewhere in the same scope, the shadowing causes a confusing `TypeError` or silent misbehavior. Fix: rename the local variable to avoid shadowing.

title: unused variable assignment (W0612, line 1075)
detail: Variable assigned at line 1075 is never used. Dead assignments may indicate a forgotten use. Fix: remove the assignment or prefix with `_`.

title: 3× unused argument (W0613) — e.g. `instance`, `ignore_missing_network_data`, `context`
detail: 3 function arguments are never used within their function bodies. This often signals an interface mismatch or a method that should be `@staticmethod`. Fix: use the argument, or prefix with `_` if it's an intentionally unused interface slot.
